stated: Reform UK will cut the foreign aid budget by 50%, saving £6 billion, and undertake a major review of its effectiveness, including payments to global quangos.

source.quote: Cut Foreign Aid by 50% Save £6 billion from the £12.8 billion budget. A major review is needed into the effectiveness of overseas aid. That includes global quangos to which we pay over £7 billion every year.

bearing_set.reason: Foreign aid funds conflict-prevention, counter-terrorism cooperation, and stabilisation programmes that credibly feed into UK national security posture; a 50% cut is large enough to earn a non-negligible verdict on whether the country is more or less secure against external threats.

UK International Climate Finance (a significant ODA component) would be cut, directly reducing contributions to global climate action and worsening the UK's emissions-trajectory commitments under international agreements.

Cutting ODA by ~50% removes approximately £6 bn of annual spending; this directly and non-negligibly improves (or changes the funded/borrowed balance of) the fiscal position, with a concrete effect on debt-path sustainability.

membership_note: The two genuine bearings are the fiscal improvement (O12) and the reduction in climate/environment finance (O6). Possible O5 (aid-as-security-dividend) and O13 (reallocation to domestic growth) effects are too indirect and speculative without a stated reallocation mechanism to clear the non-negligible bar.
